what_happened: Main had been red since 12:55 UTC. CI's full-history check failed on the squash of PR #130, which carried the content of jobs 60r4 and sg0j. The operator diagnosed it and ran the history exemption for commit 39962ed directly, using the remedy from decisions D66/D70 (OP-11), to turn main green again. No job was attached, and Athena did not diagnose or fix the red CI itself.
cause: Athena's job ends at opening the pull request. Nothing watches CI on the PR or on main after the merge, and nothing recognises a known failure pattern. The pattern here is that a squash which carries stacked jobs' content trips the full-history check. The remedy (the history exemption) already existed as a documented operator step (D66/D70, OP-11) but is not wired to any automatic trigger. So a red main waits for a person to read the log, diagnose it and run the exemption. The stacked jobs 60r4 and sg0j let their content land through #130 with no check at merge time that the history rule would pass.
prevention: Add a post-PR CI watcher. When a job's PR or main goes red, it reads the failing check and matches it to known remedies. For the full-history failure on a squash carrying stacked jobs, it files or runs the history exemption as a tracked, logged job. For unknown failures, it opens a diagnosis job and alerts the owner. Also add a pre-merge check that a squash of stacked jobs will pass the full-history rule, or generate the exemption with the PR.
proposed_request: When a pull request opened by an Athena job, or main after its merge, fails a CI check, Athena should notice and handle it without an operator. Read the failing check's log and match it to documented remedies. For a full-history check failure caused by a squash that carries content from stacked jobs (as with #130, jobs 60r4 and sg0j, commit 39962ed), apply the history exemption from D66/D70 (OP-11) as a logged job. For any failure with no known remedy, open a diagnosis job and tell the owner. Done when: a test simulating the #130 failure gets main green with no manual step, each automatic fix is recorded, and an unknown failure produces a diagnosis job instead of waiting silently.
